Given that
$$y=3x^2+6x^{\frac{1}{3}}+\frac{2x^3-7}{3\sqrt{x}}, \quad x>0$$
find $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$. Give each term in your answer in its simplest form.
(6)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Attempts to split the fraction into 2 terms and obtains either $\alpha x^{\frac{5}{2}}$ or $\beta x^{-\frac{1}{2}}$. This may be implied by a correct power of $x$ in their differentiation of one of these terms. But beware of $\beta x^{-\frac{1}{2}}$ coming from $\frac{2x^3-7}{3\sqrt{x}}=2x^3-7+3x^{-\frac{1}{2}}$: $\frac{2x^3-7}{3\sqrt{x}}=\frac{2x^3}{3\sqrt{x}}-\frac{7}{3\sqrt{x}}=\frac{2}{3}x^{\frac{5}{2}}-\frac{7}{3}x^{-\frac{1}{2}}$.
M1: Differentiates by reducing power by one for any of their powers of $x$: $x^n \to x^{n-1}$.
A1: $6x$. Do not accept $6x^1$. Depends on second M mark only. Award when first seen and isw.
A1: $2x^{-\frac{2}{3}}$. Must be simplified so do not accept e.g. $\frac{2}{1}x^{-\frac{2}{3}}$ but allow $\frac{2}{\sqrt[3]{x^2}}$. Depends on second M mark only. Award when first seen and isw.
A1: $\frac{5}{3}x^{\frac{3}{2}}$. Must be simplified but allow e.g. $1\frac{2}{3}x^{1.5}$ or e.g. $\frac{5}{3}\sqrt{x^3}$. Award when first seen and isw.
A1: $\frac{7}{6}x^{-\frac{3}{2}}$. Must be simplified but allow e.g. $1\frac{1}{6}x^{-1.5}$ or e.g. $\frac{7}{6\sqrt{x^3}}$. Award when first seen and isw.
Final answer: $\frac{dy}{dx}=6x+2x^{-\frac{2}{3}}+\frac{5}{3}x^{\frac{3}{2}}+\frac{7}{6}x^{-\frac{3}{2}}$.
In an otherwise fully correct solution, penalise the presence of $+c$ by deducting the final A1.
Use of Quotient Rule: First M1 and final A1A1 (other marks as above). M1: Uses correct quotient rule $\frac{d}{dx}\left(\frac{2x^3-7}{3\sqrt{x}}\right)=\frac{3\sqrt{x}(6x^2)-(2x^3-7)\frac{3}{2}x^{-\frac{1}{2}}}{(3\sqrt{x})^2}$. A1: Correct first term of numerator and correct denominator $=\frac{10x^{\frac{5}{2}}+7x^{-\frac{1}{2}}}{6x}$. A1: All correct as simplified as shown. So $\frac{dy}{dx}=6x+2x^{-\frac{2}{3}}+\frac{10x^{\frac{5}{2}}+7x^{-\frac{1}{2}}}{6x}$ scores full marks.
